data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Budget-exhaustion halts and crash halts must be treated differently: a budget halt is resumable if the budget check is performed atomically at event boundaries (making it a cooperative, controlled stop), whereas a crash halt (power loss, process kill, OOM) must always be refused immediate resumption and instead require an audit-then-truncate-or-restart path, because the crash may have corrupted the log tail in ways the identity chain alone cannot distinguish from a valid event.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the budget check is not atomic with respect to event commit (e.g., the system streams output and checks budget token-by-token), a budget halt can itself produce a partial write, collapsing the distinction between budget and crash halts.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the storage layer provides true atomic append semantics (e.g., a journaling filesystem with fsync, or a database with ACID transactions), then crash halts may also be clean by construction, and the distinction collapses in the other direction\u2014crash halts become resumable too.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If there is no external durable commit marker separate from the event itself, the audit path for crash halts cannot reliably distinguish a valid last event from a corrupted one, making the distinction operationally vacuous.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Cooperative budget halts are deterministic: the system chose to stop at a known-safe point, wrote a halt marker, and flushed. Crash halts are non-deterministic: the OS or hardware may have written partial sectors, reordered writes, or left the log tail in an inconsistent state that happens to hash-validate by coincidence or because the hash was computed before the body was fully persisted. Therefore, for crash halts, the system must verify the full tail event against external checkpoints (e.g., fsync confirmations, checksums over entire event bodies, or a separate durable commit marker) before deciding whether truncation is safe or a full restart is required.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
